title: Observation table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: States of matter (Marvellous Medicine and How Far Can Sound Travel?)
source: Seeded from science/y4 lesson 9 (Observation table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 9: Water in three states: observing ice, water and steam. To understand that water can change between solid, liquid and gas and stay the same substance

questions.model: Ask: does ice keep its shape? Yes. Things that keep their shape are solids. So ice is a solid.

questions.q: What happens to an ice cube left on a warm plate?
Is the steam cloud we see a gas?
questions.a: No, it is tiny drops of liquid water; the gas is invisible.

questions.q: Core: Put an ice cube on a saucer. Observe it every 5 minutes for 15 minutes. Write what you notice each time.
questions.a: For example: 0 min hard and dry; 5 min a puddle forming; 10 min smaller and rounder; 15 min mostly water.
questions.model: Teacher shows the first observation: 'At 0 minutes the ice is hard, cold and has sharp edges. There is no water on the saucer.'

questions.q: Extend: Draw the three states of water and label each one.
Stretch: Where in nature do we find water as a solid, a liquid and a gas?
questions.a: Solid: glaciers, snow; liquid: rivers, sea, rain; gas: water vapour in the air.

questions.q: Big question: is ice still water?
questions.a: Yes: it is the same substance in a different state.
